arrival.stringValue:
Technician arrived at customer’s residence and performed diagnostic service on the HVAC system. During evaluation, the system was found to be low on refrigerant.
The run capacitor was tested and found to be reading below proper microfarad range. Replaced failed capacitor with new 45/5 +5 capacitor.
Performed leak detection at time of service; no leaks were found.
Added 2 lbs of refrigerant to bring system charge closer to manufacturer-recommended operating range and achieve proper subcooling.
A blower cleaning was recommended and completed. After reinstalling the blower assembly, the blower motor faulted and failed to operate properly. Blower motor was then replaced with a new blower assembly/motor, and system operation was restored.
Installed TekAir Signature Caps on refrigerant service ports at refrigerant lines.
The following components were also checked and verified operational at time of service:
Air handler breaker/fuse: Passed
Contactor: Passed
Transformer: Passed
Recommendation: System was found low on refrigerant at time of service. Leak detection was performed with no leaks found at this visit. Continued monitoring is recommended, and further diagnostic may be needed if refrigerant loss continues.

description.stringValue:
Completed system diagnostic, refrigerant leak detection, and refrigerant recharge service.
During diagnostic, system was found low on refrigerant. Initial temperature split/delta T was approximately 11°F, indicating reduced cooling performance.
Inspected accessible refrigeration components and identified a refrigerant leak at the liquid line service port. Leak detection was also performed through the condensate line to check for signs of an evaporator coil leak; leak detection came back negative at the evaporator coil at this time.
Added 9 lbs of refrigerant to improve system operation and cooling performance. After refrigerant was added, system temperature split/delta T improved from approximately 11°F to 20°F, showing improved cooling performance at the time of service.
Also found the supply plenum ductwork is not properly sealed, causing loss of supply airflow and reduced system efficiency.
Tenant was advised to monitor system cooling performance and efficiency. If cooling issues continue or refrigerant loss persists, TekAir recommends full refrigerant recovery and nitrogen pressure testing to identify any additional or hidden refrigerant leaks.

diagnosis.stringValue:
Service Findings / Recommendation
System was found low on refrigerant. During inspection, the supply plenum ductwork was found not properly sealed, causing air loss and reduced supply airflow.
A refrigerant leak was located at the liquid line service port. The evaporator coil was checked through the condensate line using leak detection methods, and no leak was detected at the evaporator coil at this time.
Recommended that the tenant monitor system performance and cooling efficiency after repairs. If cooling issues continue or refrigerant loss persists, TekAir recommends a full refrigerant recovery and nitrogen pressure test to further identify any additional or hidden refrigerant leaks within the system.


Due to the system being low on refrigerant and an active leak being found at the service port, TekAir cannot guarantee that this is the only leak present without performing a full recovery and nitrogen pressure test. Further leak testing may be required if the system continues to lose refrigerant or does not maintain proper cooling performance.

arrival.stringValue:
Arrived on site for HVAC diagnostic. Inspected outdoor condenser and found the condenser fan motor had failed/seized and was not operating properly. Due to the fan motor failure, the condenser was unable to reject heat correctly, which can cause poor cooling performance, high system pressure, and possible compressor strain if operated.
Also inspected the outdoor condenser coil and found dirt/debris buildup restricting airflow through the coil. Performed condenser coil cleaning add-on service. Removed accessible debris and buildup, rinsed coil thoroughly, and improved airflow across the condenser coil.

diagnosis.stringValue: Replace failed condenser fan motor and verify proper system operation after repair. Continue routine condenser coil maintenance to help maintain airflow, efficiency, and reduce strain on equipment.

work.stringValue:
Arrived on site for HVAC service. Diagnosed outdoor condenser and found the condenser fan motor had failed/seized and was not operating properly. Condenser fan motor failure was preventing proper heat rejection at the outdoor unit, which can cause poor cooling performance, elevated system pressure, and possible compressor strain if system continues to operate.
Replaced failed condenser fan motor. Verified new motor was installed, wired, and operating properly. Confirmed condenser fan is now running and moving air across the outdoor condenser coil.
Also performed condenser coil cleaning add-on service. Removed accessible debris and buildup from the outdoor coil, rinsed coil thoroughly, and improved airflow through the condenser section.
After repairs were completed, system was tested for operation. Unit was verified operating after condenser fan motor replacement and condenser coil cleaning.

diagnosis.stringValue:
Upon initial inspection, the HVAC system required maintenance and further evaluation. Air handler door insulation was damaged/loose and needed repair to improve cabinet sealing. Condenser and evaporator coils showed buildup and required cleaning to improve airflow and heat transfer. Blower assembly was inspected for proper operation and overall condition.
Refrigerant levels were checked, and leak detection was performed prior to completing service work. Bubble leak detection testing was completed with negative results, and no active refrigerant leak was found at the time of inspection.

work.stringValue:
Completed refrigerant check and performed leak detection on the system. Bubble leak detection test was completed with negative results, and no active refrigerant leak was found at the time of service.
Repaired air handler door insulation to improve cabinet sealing and help reduce air loss. Cleaned condenser coil and evaporator coil to improve airflow and heat transfer. Evaluated blower operation and confirmed blower assembly was inspected for proper performance.
System was serviced, cleaned, and evaluated. Recommend continued monitoring of system performance and routine maintenance to help maintain proper operation.

completion.stringValue:
Completed HVAC system evaluation, maintenance, and minor repair work. Refrigerant check was performed, and leak detection was completed using bubble testing with negative results. No active refrigerant leak was found at the time of service.
Repaired air handler door insulation to improve cabinet sealing. Cleaned condenser and evaporator coils to improve airflow, heat transfer, and overall system performance. Evaluated blower operation for proper function.
System was operating at completion of service. Recommend customer continue to monitor system performance and schedule routine maintenance to help prevent future issues.

thankYouNote.stringValue: Thank you so much for your business! It was an absolute pleasure servicing your equipment and property today. If you have any questions, please reach out to us.

description.stringValue: Performed HVAC system evaluation and maintenance. Checked refrigerant levels and completed leak detection inspection, including bubble leak detection testing with negative results. Evaluated blower operation and overall system performance. No active refrigerant leak was found at the time of service.

name.stringValue: HVAC System Service, Coil Cleaning & Leak Detection

description.stringValue:
Cleaned condenser coil and evaporator coil to improve airflow and heat transfer. 
Repaired air handler door insulation to improve cabinet sealing.

recommendations.stringValue:
During inspection, the air handler was found to be in poor overall condition with heavy debris accumulation, biological growth, corrosion, and deterioration inside the cabinet, blower assembly, electrical compartment, and evaporator coil area.
Due to the age and condition of the equipment, replacement of the air handler and matched outdoor condenser is recommended. This is recommended to improve system reliability, airflow, efficiency, indoor air quality, and safe operation.

There is also concern with the electrical/breaker area being covered with debris, which should be addressed due to potential safety and overheating concerns.

description.stringValue: Performed full system diagnostic on non-operational HVAC system. Checked thermostat operation, low-voltage wiring, system response, air handler condition, electrical components, and refrigerant readings. Found system operational after thermostat and wiring issues were addressed. Customer was advised of air handler condition and replacement recommendation due to age, contamination, deterioration, and safety concerns.

Replaced faulty thermostat and repaired thermostat power/control wiring issue. Restored proper low-voltage communication between the thermostat and HVAC system. Tested operation and confirmed system is responding properly to thermostat commands.
Courtesy discount applied at vendor discretion.

arrival.stringValue: Arrived on site to find the HVAC system completely non-operational. Began diagnostic troubleshooting and confirmed the system was not responding to thermostat commands. During inspection, found the thermostat to be faulty and also identified issues with the thermostat power wiring preventing proper control voltage operation. Further diagnostics were performed to isolate the control circuit issue and verify system response.

diagnosis.stringValue:
Found the HVAC system non-operational upon arrival. During diagnostic testing, confirmed the thermostat was faulty and not properly sending calls for operation. Also found issues with the thermostat power/control wiring, which was preventing proper low-voltage communication between the thermostat and HVAC equipment.
After further troubleshooting, the system required thermostat replacement and correction of the thermostat wiring issue to restore proper operation.

work.stringValue: Replaced the faulty thermostat and corrected the thermostat power/control wiring issue. Verified proper low-voltage wiring connections and restored communication between the thermostat and HVAC equipment. Tested system operation after repairs and confirmed the equipment responded properly to thermostat commands.

completion.stringValue:
Checked refrigerant operating pressures/readings during system operation. Readings were within operational range at the time of service. System was functioning properly after thermostat replacement and wiring repair, with no additional operational issues found during final testing.
Customer was advised that the existing HVAC system is in poor overall condition. Inspection found heavy biological growth, debris accumulation, corrosion, and deterioration throughout the air handler, blower assembly, electrical compartment, and evaporator coil area.
The blower motor and blower assembly are heavily contaminated, which can restrict airflow, reduce efficiency, place additional strain on system components, and negatively affect indoor air quality. The electrical compartment and breaker area also show excessive debris buildup, creating a potential safety concern due to limited visibility, contamination around electrical components, and possible overheating or electrical failure risk.
Due to the age, condition, contamination level, and safety concerns observed, replacement of the air handler and matched outdoor condenser is recommended to restore proper airflow, reliability, efficiency, indoor air quality, and safe system operation.

added 4 lbs of refrigerant to the HVAC system to improve cooling performance and restore proper operation.
Labor to evaluate cooling performance, add refrigerant to system, and verify operation after charging. Temperature split improved from approximately 12°F to 19°F after refrigerant was added.

arrival.stringValue: Arrived on site to evaluate cooling performance. Customer reported unit was not cooling properly. Began system inspection by checking thermostat operation, indoor air temperature, supply air temperature, and overall system performance. Initial temperature split measured approximately 12°F, indicating reduced cooling performance.

diagnosis.stringValue:
System is operating with reduced cooling performance. Temperature split measured approximately 12°F, which is below the expected cooling range. Based on system operation and readings, the unit appears to be low on refrigerant and will need refrigerant added to restore proper cooling performance.
Recommendation:
Add refrigerant as needed and recheck system operation after charging. If refrigerant loss continues, leak detection should be performed to locate the source of the refrigerant loss.

work.stringValue: Added 4 lbs of refrigerant to the system due to low cooling performance. Initial temperature split was approximately 12°F. After refrigerant was added, system operation was rechecked and temperature split improved to approximately 19°F. Unit was cooling properly at time of completion.

completion.stringValue:
System is operational and cooling at this time. Supply and return air temperatures showed an improved temperature split after refrigerant charge adjustment. Customer was advised that if refrigerant loss continues, leak detection may be required to identify the source of the leak.
Recommendations:
Condenser coil is recommended for an acid wash / chemical coil cleaning due to buildup restricting heat transfer and reducing system efficiency. Cleaning the condenser coil will help improve airflow, system performance, and cooling operation.
Blower assembly is also recommended for service due to residue buildup on the blower wheel. Buildup on the blower wheel can reduce airflow, lower cooling performance, increase system strain, and cause uneven comfort issues.

The purpose of this visit is to review the existing rooftop equipment, verify visible conditions, document findings, and prepare recommended next steps for repair pricing or project planning. 

Included Site Visit Scope 
• Review and visually inspect the seven listed rooftop units. 
• Verify accessible equipment information and general rooftop conditions. 
• Take photos of equipment, nameplates where accessible, and visible deficiencies. • Review service access and identify obvious safety or access concerns. 
• Document visible conditions related to filters, coils, wiring, panels, and major components. 
• Prepare recommendations for repair pricing, follow-up diagnostics, or next steps. 

Excluded From Site Visit Price This site visit price does not include repairs, parts, refrigerant, refrigerant recovery, leak searches, coil cleaning, filter replacement, electrical repairs, lift/crane rental, after-hours service, or major diagnostic testing. Proposal pricing is based on normal business hours and reasonable rooftop access.

work.stringValue:
Arrived on site for emergency HVAC service call. Inspected system operation and found unit low on R-22 refrigerant. Added refrigerant to improve system cooling operation. System appears to have a refrigerant leak due to low charge condition. Refrigerant added today is a temporary measure and does not repair the leak.
Recommend follow-up visit to add fluorescent leak dye, allow dye to circulate, and perform a thorough leak detection to locate the source of refrigerant loss. Repair options will be provided once the leak is confirmed.

completion.stringValue:
Most critical units identified: 15, 6, 12, and 16.

Due to the age and current condition of the equipment, we recommend performing a full service on all units to give the systems the best opportunity to continue operating reliably.

These units are older and at higher risk for failure. Waiting for a complete breakdown is not recommended. Due to the age of the equipment, we also recommend more frequent observation and monitoring to help identify potential issues before they lead to major failures.

Continued monitoring, routine service, and close surveillance should be maintained to help reduce downtime and keep the units operating as long as possible.

diagnosis.stringValue:
During today’s service visit, the system was inspected due to intermittent shutdown and poor cooling performance.

When Y, G, and R were jumped at the low-voltage circuit, the system operated. This indicates the equipment can run when a cooling call is manually forced, but the normal control circuit is not consistently keeping the system energized. Further low-voltage troubleshooting may be needed to confirm whether the issue is related to the thermostat, control wiring, safety circuit, float switch, pressure switch, or control board.

While operating, the Thermal Expansion Valve was showing critical signs of failure. The TXV was freezing, and system superheat was extremely high. Normal superheat range is typically around 8–12°F, depending on equipment and operating conditions. Excessively high superheat indicates the evaporator coil is being starved of refrigerant, which can be caused by a restricted or failing TXV.

Based on these findings, replacement of the TXV is recommended. After replacement, the system should be evacuated, recharged as needed, and fully tested to verify proper superheat, subcooling, temperature split, and normal system operation.

Important note: The unit should not be left operating with Y, G, and R jumped. Jumping the circuit is for testing purposes only and may bypass normal controls or safety protections.

diagnosis.stringValue:
Upon arrival, the compressor was not operating and was found overheated. Electrical diagnostics were performed on the compressor, including winding resistance and ground checks. Compressor windings tested within expected resistance ranges, and no short to ground was detected. The low-pressure safety switch was closed, and proper line voltage was verified at the contactor.
Further inspection found an incorrectly sized 30/5 µF dual-run capacitor installed. The system requires a 40/5 µF capacitor. The incorrect capacitor was replaced with the proper size, and compressor operation was restored.

work.stringValue:
Recovered the existing R-410A refrigerant charge and removed the failed TXV and liquid-line filter drier. Installed a new HXCAE-6-KX-ODF TXV and ICP 163S filter drier, Mfg. #1056378. Dry nitrogen was flowed during brazing to reduce oxidation and internal contamination.
Pressure-tested the sealed HVAC system with dry nitrogen and verified no leaks were detected. Evacuated the system and confirmed vacuum stability before restarting the unit.
Returned the unit to operation and adjusted the R-410A refrigerant charge. Final operating readings showed approximately 128 psig suction pressure, 375 psig discharge pressure, 15.3°F superheat, and 8°F subcooling. Verified the unit was operating properly following the repair.

completion.stringValue:
Recovered the existing R-410A refrigerant charge and removed the failed TXV and liquid-line filter drier. Installed a new HXCAE-6-KX-ODF TXV and ICP 163S filter drier, Mfg. #1056378. Dry nitrogen was flowed during brazing to help prevent internal oxidation and contamination.
Pressure-tested the sealed HVAC system with dry nitrogen and verified no leaks were detected. Evacuated the system, confirmed vacuum stability, restarted the unit, and adjusted the refrigerant charge as needed.
Final operating readings were approximately 128 psig suction pressure, 375 psig discharge pressure, 15.3°F superheat, and 8°F subcooling. System operation was verified following completion of the repair.

Performed residential condenser system diagnosis after finding the 3.2 amp low-voltage control fuse open. specialInstructions.stringValue:
N/A

[Diagnostic Notes from Job #705792]:
During today’s service visit, the system was inspected due to intermittent shutdown and poor cooling performance.

When Y, G, and R were jumped at the low-voltage circuit, the system operated. This indicates the equipment can run when a cooling call is manually forced, but the normal control circuit is not consistently keeping the system energized. Further low-voltage troubleshooting may be needed to confirm whether the issue is related to the thermostat, control wiring, safety circuit, float switch, pressure switch, or control board.

While operating, the Thermal Expansion Valve was showing critical signs of failure. The TXV was freezing, and system superheat was extremely high. Normal superheat range is typically around 8–12°F, depending on equipment and operating conditions. Excessively high superheat indicates the evaporator coil is being starved of refrigerant, which can be caused by a restricted or failing TXV.

Based on these findings, replacement of the TXV is recommended. After replacement, the system should be evacuated, recharged as needed, and fully tested to verify proper superheat, subcooling, temperature split, and normal system operation.

Important note: The unit should not be left operating with Y, G, and R jumped. Jumping the circuit is for testing purposes only and may bypass normal controls or safety protections.

2. Compensation

Company agrees to pay Representative commissions based on the current Commission Schedule:

  • Base Commission: 25.0% of first-year revenue collected.
  • Accelerator: 30.0% for revenue above annual quota of $500,000.
  • Renewal: 5.0% on subscription renewals.

Representative agrees to keep all customer data, pricing strategies, and proprietary information confidential.
